subject: Civil Engineering
title: Water Treatment: From River to Tap
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Water Treatment: From River to Tap.

hook.text: The water in your glass was in a river yesterday. Treatment made it safe to drink.

buildup.text: Coagulation clumps tiny particles together. Flocculation grows the clumps larger.

discovery.text: Sedimentation lets clumps settle to the bottom. Filtration catches what remains.

twist.text: Disinfection with chlorine kills bacteria — but too much chlorine creates harmful byproducts.

climax.text: Modern plants use UV light and ozone — disinfection without chemical residues.

punchline.text: Clean water is engineering at its most essential — invisible but lifesaving.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of coagulation in water treatment?
options: To kill bacteria and viruses in the water
To clump tiny suspended particles together so they can be removed
To add minerals that improve the taste of drinking water
